mainTopic: אונס and אסמכתא in conditions (the ferry case, רב הונא's case, and the final הלכה), and the opening of the משנה about false vows made to dangerous people
overview: This amud finishes a discussion about conditions that a person fails to meet because of אונס, circumstances beyond his control. First the גמרא explains that a גט given 'if I die' works, because the husband wanted it to work even in the case of death. Then it challenges רבא from שמואל's ruling about a man stopped by a ferry, whose גט still took effect. It answers that a foreseeable obstacle like a ferry is different, because he should have planned for it. Next the גמרא asks how רב הונא's ruling can work, since it looks like an אסמכתא, a promise made without full intent. Deposited documents alone are not enough, as a משנה in בבא בתרא shows. What makes רב הונא's case binding is that the man said outright that his rights should be cancelled. The הלכה is that an אסמכתא works, as long as he was not held back by אונס and the קנין was made in an important בית דין. Finally a new משנה begins: one may make a false vow to murderers, robbers, or tax collectors to protect himself, and בית שמאי start their view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He would have given the divorce right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: in the case of 'this is a גט if I die,' the husband really wanted the גט to work even in the case of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if he had known that he would die, he would have made up his mind right away and given the גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the question of why a גט given 'if I die' takes effect even though death is an אונס. The husband would have happily given it right away if he had known he would die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death here is exactly the situation the husband was planning for, so you cannot say he 'did not mean it' for an אונס case. Since he gave the גט in the first place to protect her, he clearly wanted it to work even in this case. That is different from a man who loses his own rights through an אונס, which he never wanted.

keyTerms.meaning: Immediately, right away
He made up his mind and finalized the decision
A bill of divorce (גט)

phrases.english: For if he had known that he would die,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband from the earlier case who said, 'This is your גט if I die.'

phrases.aramaic: מִן לְאַלְתַּר הֲוָה גָּמַר וְיָהֵיב גִּיטָּא.
phrases.english: he would have immediately finalized it and given the bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that began before this section, defending רבא's view that אונס exempts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by the person's intent: the husband wanted the גט to work even in the case of death.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Death is an אונס, so the גט should not take effect, just as אונס cancels other conditions.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband would have given the גט right away had he known he would die, so the גט takes effect.

steps.title: The man who was stopped by the ferry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from a case where שמואל ruled that a man blocked by a ferry still did not count as having arrived, so the גט took effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from the man who said: 'If I do not come back within thirty days, let this be a גט'? He came, but the ferry kept him from crossing. He shouted: 'See that I came! See that I came!' And שמואל said: That is not called coming. Why? He was stopped by אונס!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case that seems to contradict רבא, who holds that a person stopped by אונס is not held to his condition. שמואל ruled that the man blocked by the ferry lost, and the גט took effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man clearly tried to come back on time and was stopped only by the ferry, a classic אונס. Even so, שמואל said the condition was not met. If אונס really cancels a condition, as רבא holds, why didn't it help here?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (used to compare two cases)
A ferry or river crossing
It cut him off, stopped him
An arrival, a coming
He was truly forced by circumstances beyond his control

phrases.english: What is different from that man who said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' are the messengers he gave the גט to.

phrases.english: If I do not come back from now
until thirty days, let it be a bill of divorce.
He came, but the ferry cut him off.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: חֲזוֹ דַּאֲתַאי, חֲזוֹ דַּאֲתַאי!
phrases.english: He said to them: See that I have come, see that I have come!
And שמואל said: That is not called coming.
phrases.notes: So he counts as not having come back in time, and the גט takes effect.

phrases.english: Why? But he was forced by circumstances beyond his control!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבא from the 'if I die' case, the גמרא raises a new case against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a person stopped by אונס is exempt from his condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל ruled that a man blocked by a ferry, a clear אונס, still failed the condition, so the גט took effect. That seems to show that אונס does not cancel a condition.

steps.title: An obvious, expected obstacle is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a ferry is a common, foreseeable obstacle, so the man should have planned for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps an אונס that is common and expected is different, and a ferry is that kind of אונס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by suggesting that a predictable obstacle like a ferry is not the kind of אונס that cancels a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a ferry might be on the other side of the river. Since the man could have expected this, he should have spelled it out in his condition. Because he did not, he is held to his words. רבא's rule still applies to surprising, unexpected אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (a suggested answer)
An obvious, foreseeable אונס
Is different

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important split between unexpected אונס, which can cancel a condition, and foreseeable אונס, which a person is expected to plan for.

phrases.english: Perhaps an apparent, foreseeable circumstance beyond one's control is different,
and a ferry is an apparent kind of obstacle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from שמואל's ferry case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between kinds of אונס: foreseeable versus unforeseeable.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any אונס, even a ferry, should cancel the condition, so שמואל contradicts רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: A foreseeable obstacle like a ferry should have been planned for, so it does not cancel the condition. רבא's rule applies to unexpected אונס.

steps.title: Isn't רב הונא's case an empty promise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב הונא could say the man loses his rights, since his condition looks like an אסמכתא, which does not create a binding transfer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב הונא: after all, it is an אסמכתא, and an אסמכתא does not make a transfer binding!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רב הונא, who ruled that the man who missed his deadline loses his court rights. It asks how that can be, since the condition looks like an אסמכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a promise a person makes because he is sure he will never have to keep it. Here the man was sure he would come back on time, so he never truly meant to give up his rights. Normally such a promise does not take effect, so why does רב הונא say he loses?

keyTerms.meaning: After all, since (introduces an obvious point)
A promise made without full intent, because the person is sure the condition will never happen
Does not effect a binding acquisition or transfer

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not about אונס at all. Even if the man had simply been lazy and missed the deadline, the problem of אסמכתא would still apply.

phrases.english: And according to רב הונא, after all, it is an אסמכתא.
phrases.notes: רב הונא is the one from earlier who ruled that the man who missed his deadline loses his court rights.

phrases.english: And an אסמכתא does not effect acquisition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אונס discussion and goes back to examine רב הונא's ruling from another angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the man's court rights are lost when he misses his deadline.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The man was sure he would return, so his promise to give up his rights was an אסמכתא. An אסמכתא does not take effect, so his rights should not be lost.

steps.title: His documents were deposited in court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this case is different because the man's court documents were already being held, which shows he truly meant to give them up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because his court documents were being held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the אסמכתא question: the man had already handed over his documents to be held, so his promise was serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a person deposits his documents with the court, he has shown real commitment, and his promise is not just empty words. So the problem of אסמכתא does not apply, and רב הונא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, in this case
Are being held, deposited
His rights, meaning the documents that prove his case

steps.whatToRemember: Two ideas so far: (1) A גט 'if I die' works because the husband wanted it even in the case of death. (2) A foreseeable אונס like a ferry does not cancel a condition, because the person should have planned for it. The answer about deposited documents is challenged right away in Step 6, and Step 7 gives the real distinction.

phrases.english: Here it is different, because his rights are being held.
phrases.notes: His papers proving his case were left with the court, so he really meant what he said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אסמכתא challenge against רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the documents were deposited, which shows full intent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man's condition is an אסמכתא and should not take effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because his documents were held by the court, he truly committed, so it is not an אסמכתא and he loses his rights. Step 6 challenges this, and Step 7 gives the final distinction.

steps.title: A held document is still an אסמכתא in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: is having the documents held really enough to stop it from being an אסמכתא? A משנה about a debtor who left his loan document with a third party shows it is still an אסמכתא, and רב rules that an אסמכתא does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where the documents are being held, is it not an אסמכתא? But we learned in a משנה: Someone paid back part of his debt and left the loan document with a third person. He said: 'If I don't pay the rest within thirty days, give the lender his document.' The time came and he did not pay. רבי יוסי says: give it. רבי יהודה says: don't give it. And רב said: the הלכה is not like רבי יוסי, who holds that an אסמכתא works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 5, which said that because the documents were being held, the man really meant it. It brings a משנה where a document was also held by someone else, yet it still counted as an אסמכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה the debtor also handed over his document, just like the man in רב הונא's case. Still, רב rules against רבי יוסי, which means an אסמכתא does not work even when a document is being held. So holding the documents alone cannot be what makes רב הונא's case binding.

keyTerms.meaning: A promise made with confidence that the condition will never happen, so the person never truly meant to pay
Are being held (by a third party or the court)
But didn't we learn in a משנה? (opens a challenge from a משנה)
Left something with a third person for safekeeping
A written document, here a loan document

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who loses here. The debtor already paid part, so if the document goes to the lender, the lender can collect the whole amount again. That is the penalty the debtor agreed to, which is why it looks like an אסמכתא.

phrases.english: And where [the documents] are being held,
is it not an אסמכתא?
phrases.notes: This questions the answer from Step 5, that held documents show he truly meant it.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
phrases.notes: The משנה is in בבא בתרא 168a.

phrases.english: One who paid back part of his debt,
and left his loan document with a third person,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: אִם אֵין אֲנִי נוֹתֵן לוֹ
phrases.english: and said: If I do not give him [the rest]
from now until thirty days,
give him [the lender] his document.
The time came and he did not pay,
רבי יוסי says: He should give [the document to the lender].
And רבי יהודה says: He should not give it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה, in the name of רב:
The הלכה is not like רבי יוסי,
who said that an אסמכתא works!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא דְּמִיתַּפְסִין לָאו אַסְמַכְתָּא הִיא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 5, which said held documents show real intent.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 5 that held documents stop the case from being an אסמכתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה the document was also held by a third party, and רב still rules it is an אסמכתא that does not work.

steps.title: Here he openly said his rights should be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב הונא's case is different because the man clearly said his winning documents should be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because he said his documents of rights should be cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a difference between the משנה and רב הונא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the debtor only left his document with someone. In רב הונא's case, the man also stated outright that his rights should be cancelled if he did not come. That clear statement shows he truly meant it, so it is not treated like an ordinary אסמכתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different here
They should be cancelled
His documents of rights (the papers showing he won)

phrases.english: It is different here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means רב הונא's case from Step 4, not the משנה.

phrases.english: because he said his documents of rights should be cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by pointing out a difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: in רב הונא's case he explicitly said his rights should be cancelled.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Held documents alone might seem to make it binding, but the משנה shows they don't.
steps.terutzMaskana: What makes רב הונא's case binding is the man's clear statement that his rights should be cancelled.

steps.title: Final ruling: an אסמכתא works, with two conditions
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that an אסמכתא works, but only if the person was not held back by forces beyond his control, and only if the קנין was done in an important בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: an אסמכתא works. But only where he was not forced by circumstances, and only where they made a קנין with him in an important בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion by giving the practical הלכה about אסמכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רב ruled against רבי יוסי, the final הלכה is that an אסמכתא does work. It has two conditions: the person must not have been prevented by something out of his control, and the agreement must have been made with a קנין before an important בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical ruling
It works to transfer ownership
Forced or held back by circumstances beyond his control
A formal act that makes a transfer or obligation binding
An important, respected court

steps.whatToRemember: An אסמכתא works only if (1) the person was not held back by forces beyond his control, and (2) the קנין was made in an important בית דין.
steps.confusionAlert: This seems to go against רב, who said the הלכה is not like רבי יוסי. The final הלכה does say an אסמכתא works, but only with these two conditions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for any business deal or penalty clause that depends on a condition the person never expected to happen.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: an אסמכתא works.
But only where he was not held back by forces beyond his control,
phrases.notes: An obstacle he could not control would excuse him. The גמרא here does not say whether a foreseeable obstacle, like the ferry in Step 3, would also count.

phrases.english: and only where they made a קנין with him
in an important בית דין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion with the final practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An אסמכתא works, as long as the person was not held back by forces beyond his control and the קנין was made in an important בית דין.

steps.title: You may make a false vow to protect yourself from dangerous people
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person may vow falsely to murderers, robbers, or tax collectors, claiming his produce is תרומה or belongs to the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may make a vow to murderers, robbers, and tax collectors that his produce is תרומה, even though it is not. He may also vow that his things belong to the king's household, even though they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It teaches that when dangerous people threaten someone's life or property, he is allowed to make a false vow to get rid of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person must be very careful with vows and must never lie with one. Here the משנה allows it because he is under pressure, and a vow like this does not count as a real vow. Claiming the produce is תרומה or that it belongs to the king's house is meant to make these dangerous people leave his property alone.

keyTerms.meaning: One may take a vow
Murderers: people who might kill someone over money
Robbers or bandits
Tax collectors, often greedy and unfair
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן; a non-כהן may not eat it
The king's household or government

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying lying is fine in general. It only allows this false vow when someone is in danger from people like murderers, robbers, or unfair tax collectors.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the topic of vows made under pressure (אונס). It shows that a vow forced out of someone by danger does not have the full power of a normal vow.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may take a vow to murderers
and to robbers and to tax collectors
that it is תרומה,
phrases.notes: He means the produce he is carrying. The robber won't take it, since only a כהן may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: even though it is not תרומה.
that they belong to the house of the king,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן שֶׁל בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ.
phrases.english: even though they do not belong to the house of the king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the אסמכתא discussion ended in step 8. It is a new topic: vows made under pressure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may make a false vow to murderers, robbers, or tax collectors, saying his produce is תרומה or belongs to the king, to protect himself and his property.

steps.title: בית שמאי begin their view on what kind of vow may be used
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי start to say that in such a case a person may vow using any form of vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: One may vow in any way...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the opinion of בית שמאי about these pressured vows. Their statement starts here and continues in the next part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said a false vow to dangerous people is allowed. בית שמאי now speak about how far that permission goes: which wordings or kinds of vows may be used. The details of their view and the limits come in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: The students of שמאי, a school of Sages who often argue with בית הלל
With everything: using any form or wording of a vow

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
One may vow using every form of vow,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the opinion of בית שמאי on how the permission in step 9 may be carried out. Their statement continues past this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי hold that, in a case of danger, one may make the false vow using any form of vow (the rest of their statement follows).
